Figure 4: Separable Convolutions Speedup on 3D Volume
Paper: "DeepTensor: Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition with Deep Network Priors" (Section 3.2, Page 4)

Compares:
1. Three 1D DIP networks: f_U(z_U) (x) f_V(z_V) (x) f_W(z_W)
2. One 2D DIP + One 1D DIP network: f_UV(z_UV) (x) f_W(z_W)
3. One full 3D ConvNet DIP network: f_UVW(z_UVW)

Plots MSE vs Wall-Clock Training Time (seconds) to empirically demonstrate
the ~2 orders of magnitude speedup offered by dimensionality splitting.

Figure 4 Improved Benchmark: Separable Convolutions Speedup on 3D Volume
Paper: "DeepTensor: Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition with Deep Network Priors" (Section 3.2, Page 4 & Figure 4)

Target Specifications:
- Volume: 3D MRI volume size: 128 x 128 x 150 (2,457,600 voxels), correcting previous 64 x 64 x 32 toy volume.
- Compares:
  1. Three 1D DIP networks: f_U(z_U) (x) f_V(z_V) (x) f_W(z_W)
  2. One 2D DIP + One 1D DIP network: f_UV(z_UV) (x) f_W(z_W)
  3. One full 3D ConvNet DIP network: f_UVW(z_UVW)
- Rationale for Speedup:
  Separable dimensionality splitting reduces convolutional FLOPs from O(H W D K^3 C^2)
  down to O((H + W + D) K C^2), achieving ~2 orders of magnitude speedup on standard GPU hardware.
- Outputs:
  - figure4_improved_benchmark_metrics.json
  - plots/figure4_separable_convolutions_speedup_improved.png
  - progression_time_vs_mse.csv

Figure 13(a): Effect of Rank Choice on Hyperspectral Image Decomposition
Paper: "DeepTensor: Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition with Deep Network Priors" (Section 4.4, Page 9-10)

Experiment:
- ICVL Hyperspectral Image truncated to Rank-20 ground truth (174, 164, 260)
- Measurement Noise: Poisson (tau=100) + Gaussian (snr=2) -> Input PSNR ~ 25 dB
- Decomposition Rank swept from 1 to 30: [1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30]
- Evaluates DeepTensor vs Truncated SVD to demonstrate that DeepTensor is insensitive
  to rank over-estimation due to its deep network prior.

Figure 10: 3-Way PARAFAC Tensor Denoising on Extended Yale Face Database B
Paper: "DeepTensor: Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition with Deep Network Priors" (Section 4.1, Page 7-8)

Dataset: Extended Yale Face B (data/yale_b.mat) -> (192, 168, 160)
Corruption: 30% and 60% Salt-and-Pepper impulse noise
Model: 3-Way PARAFAC Decomposition with Deep Network Priors (Rank R=2000)
       Mode 1 (Height H=192): 1D Deep Image Prior U_net
       Mode 2 (Width W=168): 1D Deep Image Prior V_net
       Mode 3 (Images/Slices T=160): 1D Deep Image Prior W_net
       Core tensor lambda of size (R,)
Loss: L1 norm penalty (robust to spatially sparse impulse noise)
Baselines: Truncated SVD, Classical PARAFAC, KDRSDL comparison

Figure 10 Improved Rerun: 3-Way PARAFAC Tensor Denoising on Extended Yale Face Database B
Paper: "DeepTensor: Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition with Deep Network Priors" (Section 4.1, Page 7-8)

Improvements Implemented:
1. Exact Noise Protocol: Vectorized exact fixed corruption percentage (and Bernoulli option)
   eliminating coordinate collisions that corrupted only ~25.8% and ~44.9% in the old run.
2. Architecture Scaling: 128 channels per scale (skip_n33d=128, skip_n33u=128) across 5 scales,
   providing full paper-specified capacity (1.82M params per 1D U-Net vs 0.46M in 64-channel baseline).
3. Convergence Budget: Extended training up to 5,000 epochs with Cosine Annealing scheduler.
4. Independent Execution: Strict separation between 30% and 60% noise regimes.
5. Rigorous Telemetry: Full tracking of peak GPU VRAM, wall-clock time, loss history, and PSNR progression.

Figure 13(b): Effect of Rank Choice on PARAFAC Tensor Decomposition (Yale Face B)
Paper: "DeepTensor: Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition with Deep Network Priors" (Section 4.4, Page 9-10)

Experiment:
- Yale Face B tensor (192, 168, 160) truncated to Rank-1000 PARAFAC ground truth.
- Measurement Noise: Poisson (tau=100) + Gaussian (snr=2) -> Input PSNR ~ 25 dB
- Decomposition Rank swept from 10 to 4000: [10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000]
- Evaluates DeepTensor vs Truncated Tensor Decomposition (PARAFAC/SVD) to demonstrate that
  DeepTensor reaches a plateau above the true rank, while classical PARAFAC degrades sharply.

Figure 13(b) Improved Rerun: Effect of Rank Choice on PARAFAC Tensor Decomposition (Yale Face B)
Paper: "DeepTensor: Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition with Deep Network Priors" (Section 4.4, Page 9-10)

Key Improvements Implemented:
1. True 3-Way PARAFAC Alternating Least Squares (ALS) Baseline:
   Mathematically exact, vectorized PyTorch CUDA implementation of classical unregularized PARAFAC ALS.
   Eliminates the matricized SVD proxy and the artificial logarithm penalty from the previous script.
2. Extended Convergence Budget:
   Trained for 1,500 epochs per rank (increased from under-converged 500 epochs), allowing DeepTensor
   to reach its genuine asymptotic reconstruction plateau (~26 dB).
3. Strict Ground-Truth Isolation:
   Checkpoints and best reconstructions are selected strictly by minimum training loss (Rule 9).
   Ground-truth tensor is used strictly for post-hoc evaluation.
4. Comprehensive Artifact Generation:
   Saves rank-wise progression CSV, visual panels across key ranks (10, 500, 1000, 4000),
   intermediate checkpoints, and publication-ready comparative plots.

Figure 11 Improved Rerun: Video Compressive Sensing
Paper: "DeepTensor: Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition with Deep Network Priors" (Section 4.3, Page 7 & 9)

Dataset: Cat Video (data/cat_video.mat) -> (128, 128, 64)
Forward Model: Random pixel-wise spatial-multiplexing coded aperture (Hitomi et al., ICCV 2011)
Combining nframes=8 frames into 1 coded image snapshot (8 total snapshots).

Improvements over Previous Baseline:
1. Rank Scaling: Set to full-rank R=64 (previous baseline was bottlenecked at R=32).
2. Convergence Budget: Extended to full paper-specified 10,000 epochs (previous baseline stopped at 3,000).
3. Network Capacity: 128 channels per scale in 2D spatial DIP and 1D temporal DIP (previous baseline had 64).
4. TV Baseline Calibration: 2D TV baseline calibrated with 1,000 epochs to match paper's 24.10 dB reference.
5. Strict Separation & Telemetry: Preserves original baseline, tracks full loss & PSNR progression, VRAM, and runtime.

Figure 12 Improved Rerun: 3D PET CT Volume Reconstruction from Limited, Noisy Tomography
Paper: "DeepTensor: Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition with Deep Network Priors" (Section 4.1, Page 8-9)

Target Paper Element: Figure 12 & Section 4.1
- Volume: data/pet.mat (128 x 128 x 56)
- Measurements: Radon transform along 40 angles (0 to 180 degrees)
- Decomposition: Rank-1000 PARAFAC tensor (3x 1D DIP networks with positional encoding)
- Measurement Noise: Poisson (tau=100, paper-aligned) + Gaussian readout (snr=2)
- Training Budget: 4,000 epochs (extended from 2,000 for asymptotic convergence)
- Checkpoint Selection: Strictly by minimum measurement loss (Rule 9 / GT isolation)
- Baselines:
  1. Algorithmic Inversion (Linear gradient descent, no prior)
  2. 2D Total Variation (TV) Regularization
  3. DeepTensor (Rank-1000 PARAFAC with deep network priors)

Research Extension 1: Adaptive Rank Selection — Plateau-Based

Based on the validated DeepTensor baseline (commit a146cc7).
This script implements adaptive rank selection using a plateau-based
mechanism. Instead of fixing rank=20, the effective rank starts small
and grows when the reconstruction loss plateaus.

Core approach:
- Networks are initialized with R_MAX output channels (over-parameterization)
- During reconstruction, only the first 'current_rank' channels are used
  via tensor slicing after the full forward pass
- Inactive output channels are excluded from the reconstruction, so the
  final output-layer weights for those channels receive zero gradient.
  Internal/shared network layers still receive gradients from the active
  channels and continue to be trained normally.
- When the EMA-smoothed L1 loss improvement plateaus, active rank increases
- At rank growth, Adam optimizer state (exp_avg, exp_avg_sq) is explicitly
  reset for the newly activated final-layer output parameters to ensure
  a clean learning start
- All previously learned parameters and optimizer states for existing
  active channels are fully preserved
- No network rebuilding or architecture changes occur at rank growth

Rank-growth decisions depend ONLY on the self-supervised L1 reconstruction
loss against the noisy observation. No clean ground-truth information is
used in any training or rank-selection decision.

Reproducibility note: No random seed is set, matching the baseline protocol.
Results are stochastic due to random noise generation, network initialization,
and input perturbation. Multiple runs are needed for statistical significance.

Branch: extension/adaptive-rank
Baseline: main / commit a146cc7

Research Extension 2: Factor Group-Sparsity (Group Lasso) Regularization

Based on the validated DeepTensor baseline (commit a146cc7) and PROJECT_CONTEXT.md.
This script implements Factor Group-Sparsity (Group Lasso) regularization on the
original unnormalized DeepTensor factor matrices U and V.

Core approach:
- Original unnormalized DeepTensor architecture: Y_hat = U V^T
- Over-parameterized capacity: R_MAX = 30
- Joint factor norm for component r: g_r = sqrt(||U_r||_2^2 + ||V_r||_2^2)
- Group-sparsity regularizer: R(U,V) = sum_{r=1}^{R_MAX} g_r
- Objective: L = (95% visible L1 reconstruction loss) + lambda * R(U,V)
- Held-out 5% validation framework (fixed mask, seed 42) for hyperparameter selection
- Ground-truth PSNR/SSIM/RMSE used strictly for post-hoc evaluation after model selection

Extension 3: Missing-Data / Tensor Completion Capability for DeepTensor

FROZEN DESIGN:
- Adds mask-aware reconstruction loss to evaluate DeepTensor on tensor completion.
- DeepTensor architecture is unchanged (Fixed R = 20, DIP generators).
- Data: ICVL hyperspectral image cube (1000x1000x31 or downsampled).
- Network input: Latent noise grids (im_inp, spec_inp) ONLY. The observation tensor
  is used solely as the target in loss computation.
- Missingness Masking:
  - Uses scoped NumPy RNG (default_rng(seed)) to generate nested missing masks:
    mask_missing = u < missing_ratio (80% missing superset of 50%, superset of 20%).
  - Observed entries (1 - mask_missing) are split into 95% training and 5% validation.
  - Missing entries contribute ZERO to training and validation losses.
- Checkpoint Selection: Strictly based on self-supervised validation L1 loss (mask_val).
- Final Evaluation: Restores best checkpoint in train mode (im_net.train(), spec_net.train())
  and computes Full, Missing-only, and Observed-only PSNR/RMSE against clean ground truth.

This script replicates the DeepTensor results in Figure 6. The accuracy is
different from the paper as hyperspectral image was downsampled.

Extension 5: Ensemble Disagreement as a Proxy for Reconstruction Uncertainty.

Performs N=5 ensemble training of DeepTensor under fixed noisy observation (seed 42).
Evaluates empirical ensemble disagreement (std dev across members) vs true reconstruction error,
controlling for ground-truth edge magnitude.

Extension 7: Post-hoc Factor Analysis and Descriptive Visualization of DeepTensor Components.

Extracts spatial factors U and spectral factors V from frozen baseline R=20 DeepTensor on ICVL (seed 42, mixed noise).
Performs post-hoc energy-norm component ordering, progressive top-k ablation, spatial/spectral cosine similarity,
and generates four required descriptive visualizations.
